texts.facts: Accused persons JUDGMENT: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (PFA Act), alleging that the accused persons have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. The accused no. 1 is stated to be the vendor of M/s. D. L. Narula Fruit Products, of which accused no. 2 is the proprietor, from whose premises the food article, that is, 'vegetable sauce' was lifted for sampling. 2. As per the complaint, on 06.03.2009, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) R. K. Bhaskar and Field Assistant (FA) Om Prakash under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Aashish Mohan reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s. D. L. Narula Food Products, at Khasra No. 76, Village Ranhola, Nangloi, Delhi, where the accused no. 1 was found conducting business of the food articles and having stored for sale for human consumption "vegetable sauce" in sealed glass bottles of 400 gms each bearing identical label declaration. The sample of three such sealed glass bottles was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules. Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc. The price of sample was paid to the vendor. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA. Vide report dated 30.03.2009, the PA found the sample to be not conforming to the standards because acidity as acetic acid was less than the prescribed minimum limit. Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by the FI. It was found that the accused no. 2 was the proprietor of the business concern M/s. D. L. Narula Fruit Products and the product was being manufactured by the said concern itself. After completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court against both the accused persons on 06.08.2009 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act. 3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused persons were summoned vide order dated 06.08.2009. The accused persons appeared and filed an application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising right to get the second counterpart of the sample to be analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL). The application was allowed and a counterpart was sent for analysis to CFL. The CFL examined the sample and its Director gave Certificate dated 11.09.2009, opining the sample to be not conforming to the PFA Rules as acidity as acetic acid content was less than the minimum prescribed limit. 4. Based on the report of the CFL, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against both the accused persons on 16.12.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a), being violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 5. At the trial, prosecution examined three witnesses in support of its case. PW-1 FI R. K. Bhaskar, PW-2 Sh. Aashish Mohan (SDM/LHA) and PW-3 FA Om Prakash were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings. All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 06.03.2009 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of three sealed glass bottles 400 gms each of Vegetable Sauce bearing identical label declaration, dividing it in three parts by putting ine sealed bottle as one counterpart, separately packing, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A, cash memo Ex. PW-1/A-1, Notice in Form-VI Ex. PW-1/B (on which the vendor made endorsement that the samples were of same lot, having same batch number, having same date of manufacturing and ready for sale), Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C and Raid report Ex. PW-1/C1. The vendor accused no. 1 also furnished her statement Ex. PW-1/D and the FI also separately seized the label of the bottle Ex. PW-1/D1. They also proved the PA Receipt Ex. PW-1/E and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/F vide which the samples were deposited with the PA and SDM/LHA respectively. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the accused no. 1 did not sign the documents ir had signed under duress, or that the three samples were not of the same batch number, lot number or colour, or that representative samples were not taken, or that the accused persons had been falsely implicated. 6. Statements of the accused persons under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 23.02.2015 wherein they denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Accused no. 1 admitted the proceedings dated 06.03.2009 but stated that no effort was made to join public witnesses. Accused no. 2 on the other hand expressed ignorance about the proceedings stating that he was not present at the spot.
